title: Ghurid Dynasty
capsule: The Ghurid sultanate was an Afghan dynasty based in the mountainous Ghur region of west-central Afghanistan that rose to prominence after displacing the Ghaznavids in the mid-twelfth century. Under Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad (r. 1163-1203) and his brother Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad (r. 1173-1206), the Ghurids conquered Khurasan and extended their power deep into northern India; Mu'izz al-Din's victory at the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192 opened the Gangetic plain and laid the foundation for the Delhi Sultanate. After Mu'izz al-Din's assassination in 1206, the empire fragmented rapidly; the Khwarazmians extinguished the last Ghurid holdout in Afghanistan around 1215, while Mu'izz al-Din's slave commanders founded independent dynasties in India.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Ghurid extent is reconstructed from numismatic evidence, Persian chronicles (Juzjani's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri), and inscription records; core Afghan and Khurasanian territories are well attested, but the outer frontiers in Punjab and northern India rely heavily on narrative sources and are approximate.
